entries: From Middle High German jesen, from Old High German jesan, from Proto-Germanic *jesaną. Variants with dissimilative hardening j- → g- before front vowels occur since Middle High German. These developments were reinforced by association with the originally unrelated gar (“fully cooked”). Related to Gischt, English yeast.
